_comment: A TASK to ADD to the existing daily job — not a job to create.
The daily job already runs `dbt build --exclude tag:social`. This task goes
UPSTREAM of it, so a customer added overnight has coordinates before
int_rep_customer_presence reads them. Set your existing dbt task to
depends_on this one.
Do NOT create this as a second scheduled job that also runs dbt: two
concurrent dbt builds against the same tables will race.
WHY IT BELONGS IN THE DAILY JOB rather than its own schedule: the geocode
table is a hard dependency of int_rep_customer_presence. Split across two
schedules there is a window where a customer exists in navrep.customer with
no coordinate, and every visit to them silently reports scenario 'unknown' —
which reads as 'did not visit' to anyone who has not been told otherwise.
WHY DAILY IS CHEAP: the script is incremental on address_hash. A day with no
new customers sends zero requests and costs nothing; five new customers is
about 3 cents.
--limit 500 is a BLAST-RADIUS CAP, not a throughput setting. If an upstream
change ever rewrites every address (a formatting fix, a trailing-space
cleanup), address_hash changes for all 7,198 rows and an uncapped unattended
run would spend ~$36. Capped, the worst case is ~$2.50 and the backlog
drains over following days. Remove it only for a deliberate, attended
backfill.
SECRET: set this as an environment variable on THIS task. The value is a
reference — Databricks resolves it at runtime and redacts it from logs, so
the key never appears in the job definition, the repo, or output:
GOOGLE_GEOCODING_API_KEY = {{secrets/<scope>/google_geocoding_api_key}}
Confirm the exact reference string in the Catalog UI — the secret is stored
at ust_databricks.ust_external.google_geocoding_api_key, and UC-managed
secrets may not use the legacy {{secrets/scope/key}} form.
Databricks auth itself needs NO secret: the job's run_as identity
authenticates ambiently, and the script takes its Spark path automatically
when running on Databricks compute. run_as needs read on navrep, write on
ust_external, and read on the secret.
description: Geocode NAV customers whose address is new or changed. No-op on a quiet day.
